## Reviewer 1

### Summary

Stylus presents a framework for 3D style transfer from unposed multi-view images to a 3D scene represented by Gaussian Splatting, using a single reference style image. The core of Stylus is a Transformer-based architecture that separates content (geometry) and style information. The geometry backbone uses self-attention to predict scene structure, while style is injected via cross-attention modules that transfer style features from the reference image to the 3D representation. A novel voxel-level 3D style loss enforces view-consistent stylization by aligning feature statistics across views. The method achieves zero-shot generalization to unseen scenes and styles without per-scene optimization.
